title: Shared Swift libraries for the menu bar apps: Masthead, then LogConsole
objective: hv's four menu bar apps (menuz, Gtools.app, Intent.app and Conflab.app) share one top line and About panel, and then one log console, from this public Swift package. Each app imports only what it uses, and what the top line and the About panel say comes from files that change without a rebuild.
context:
hv, 18 Oct 2026: the four menu bar apps' top lines "all seem to be subtly different", so "normalise this functionality across the four apps into a single codebase that each one uses".

- **The top line** has two lines: a heading, which is the app's name and version, and a smaller subheading.
- **It is selectable,** and opens an About panel that renders Markdown or HTML.
- **Both are configured from files,** so a change needs no recompile.
- **It is reusable in other Swift projects,** as Arca's first Swift.

hv then folded the log console in: "Yes. Most definitely. ... And it would have: mastehead, logconsole, etc."

hv's calls:
- macOS only, with Tahoe (macOS 26) as the floor. WebKit's SwiftUI web view needs it.
- A `masthead.yaml` per app, with a default in the bundle.
- The About page in a web view, with Markdown through cmark-gfm.
- This public repo, so CI costs nothing.
- Each app's heading, subheading and own rows worked out from what it shows today.

Measured, 18 Oct:
- All four apps build the row by hand, as a disabled bold 13 pt menu item, from different sources. menuz reads its bundle's stamps, Gtools.app and Intent.app read their CLI's `version`, and Conflab.app shows the signed-in user.
- All four target macOS 14.0.
- Gtools.app's and Intent.app's consoles are separate copies that have drifted apart, at about 500 and 690 lines of Swift, and menuz was to get a third.
- Conflab.app has its own About tab in its Settings window.

`design.md` holds the design as agreed. The work packages build the package first, Masthead and then LogConsole. Each app's adoption is a work package of its own, rolled out selectively, and each is done by that project's IC from ic's brief, in its own repo and under its own gates.

criteria.text: masthead.yaml is checked against its schema. heading is required text that is not blank; subheading is text; icon is app or none, and app when it is absent; about is required, with body, the name of a .md or .html file, and css, the name of an optional .css file, each a file name with no folder in it. A key the file does not have, a value of the wrong kind, a value the key does not take and a required key that is missing are each refused in one line naming the file, the key and the value.

A masthead's values come from the bundle and from the app. The bundle gives {name}, {version}, {commit} and {kind}, from its Info.plist's CFBundleName, CFBundleShortVersionString, ArcaCommit and ArcaKind, and a stamp that is absent, empty or not text gives no value. The app names the values it gives, once, each adding a value or taking the bundle's place, and is asked for those alone. A value it names but has not got yet is missing, whatever the bundle gives.

The heading and the subheading are their templates with the values in, each line on its own. A heading with a value missing, or that comes out blank, is the app's name alone, which is its {name} value or nothing; a subheading with a value missing, or that comes out blank, is hidden. A token that names no value the app gives is refused, naming the token and the values there are.

The user's masthead.yaml is used when the app's config folder holds one that is read and checked without a refusal. One that is refused leaves the bundled default in use, and the subheading says what was wrong. With no copy that can be used, the heading is the app's name and the subheading the first refusal. Every refusal is kept, in order, for the app's log.

The About body is HTML: an about.md goes through cmark-gfm, and an about.html is used as written. Its tokens then take their values, each escaped for HTML, so a value is never markup in an element's text or a quoted attribute; a token in a Markdown link's address is left as written. The body and the stylesheet are each found as masthead.yaml is, the config folder's copy first and then the bundle's, and a copy that is refused leaves the next in use.

README.md says how masthead.yaml is written, which values its tokens take and where each comes from, the ArcaCommit and ArcaKind stamps an app's Info.plist carries among them. CHANGELOG.md says what this work package added.

attachments.text:
# ST0001 design: shared Swift libraries for the menu bar apps

As agreed with hv, 18 Oct 2026.

## The package

- **One Swift package,** `arca_swift`, for macOS 26 and later, in the Swift 6 language mode, built with the current toolchain.
- **Library products, each imported on its own:**
  - `ArcaMasthead`: the top line and the About window.
  - `ArcaLogConsole`: the log console.

  Module names carry the `Arca` prefix because a module name must be unique across an app's dependencies.
- **One internal target, `ArcaCore`,** holds what both libraries read:
  - a config file found in the app's config folder or, failing that, in its bundle;
  - YAML, read through Yams;
  - `{token}` templates.

  So neither library grows its own reader.
- **Dependencies:** Yams, and Apple's swift-cmark (cmark-gfm) for Markdown.
- **A pure core, tested with Swift Testing, and a thin AppKit and SwiftUI layer** that parses, calls and renders.
- **CI on GitHub Actions' macOS runners,** which are free for a public repo, builds and tests every push. A release is a tag, and the apps pin it.

## ArcaMasthead

### The row

- **One menu item at the top of the app's menu:** the heading as its title in bold, the subheading as its subtitle, and the app's icon as its image. macOS draws it, so highlighting, clicks and the keyboard work as for any other item. A subtitle under an attributed title shows from macOS 15.
- **It is enabled,** and choosing it opens the About window.

### The file

- **`masthead.yaml` lives in the app's config folder** (eg `~/.config/<app>/`). Without one, the default the app ships in its bundle is used. Nothing in the bundle is edited, because that breaks the app's signature.
- **A sketch of the file:**

  ```yaml
  heading: "{name} {version}"
  subheading: "{commit} · {kind}"
  icon: app
  about:
    body: about.md # or about.html
    css: about.css # optional
  ```

- **Values:**
  - The bundle gives `{name}`, `{version}`, `{commit}` and `{kind}`.
  - The app adds its own, eg `{status}` or `{user}`, through a provider that is asked at each menu open.
  - A value the app cannot give yet leaves the heading as the app's name alone.
- **The file is read again** when the menu or the About window opens, if it has changed, so nothing watches it.
- **A file that fails keeps the bundled default,** and the subheading says what is wrong. The app's log hook gets the same line.

### The About window

- **A window holding WebKit's SwiftUI web view** (`WebPage`), which needs macOS 26.
- **Markdown becomes HTML through cmark-gfm.** HTML inside Markdown passes through, so `about.html` and `about.md` take one path.
- **The page's JavaScript is off.** A link opens in the browser, the default stylesheet follows light and dark mode, and `{tokens}` expand in the body.
- **An app with no Dock icon is brought forward** to show the window.

### The four apps

| App         | Heading             | Subheading                             | Stays the app's own rows                                     |
| ----------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| menuz       | `menuz <version>`   | `<commit> · <kind>`                    | none                                                         |
| Gtools.app  | `gtools <version>`  | `<commit> · <kind>`                    | its CMS status row, which opens the site; its estate flyout  |
| Intent.app  | `intent <version>`  | `<commit> · <kind>`                    | its intentd status row, which opens the web face             |
| Conflab.app | `conflab <version>` | the signed-in user, or `not signed in` | its conflabd status row, coloured by state, in Gtools' shape |

- **Gtools.app's and Intent.app's version and commit come from their CLI** (`gtools version`, `intent version`), as today. Until the CLI answers, the heading is the app's name.
- **The build word is always named:** `release` or `dev`.
- **Conflab.app's About tab** in its Settings window becomes its `about.md`.

## ArcaLogConsole

It is reviewed before any code (WP-08), as Masthead was. The review measures how Gtools.app's and Intent.app's consoles differ, and covers:

- the CLI runs whose only output is the console, eg Run Doctor and Rebuild Search Index;
- a daemon's log, tailed while the window is open;
- menuz's run log, which must keep being followed when it is truncated or rotated under the tail.

## The work

- **ic builds the package:** WP-01 to WP-03, then WP-08 and WP-09.
- **The roll-out is selective, app by app** (WP-04 to WP-07, and WP-10). Each app's adoption is done by its own project's IC, from ic's brief, in its own repo and under its own gates. ic reviews each adoption against its brief.
- **Masthead comes first, then LogConsole.**
